common_name: Hollandia Water Lily (Double Light Pink Hardy Water Lily)

planting.note: Set the rhizome horizontally in a wide planting basket of heavy garden soil capped with gravel, then lower the container so the crown rests 18 to 30 inches beneath the water surface in full sun.

directions: Hollandia (also sold as 'Darwin') is a Dutch-bred hardy water lily prized for its large, peony-form double flowers packed with 35 or more slightly fragrant, light pink petals that fade paler toward the outer rows as the bloom ages. Its vigorous Marliac-type rhizome stays comparatively compact rather than running like the odorata or tuberosa types, making it manageable in medium to large ponds. Plant in a wide basket of heavy loam topped with gravel and site in full sun for the heaviest bloom; divide every two to three years as the crown becomes congested. Established plants can persist for a decade or more with routine feeding on aquatic fertilizer tablets through the growing season.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

common_name: Virginalis Water Lily (Classic Marliac Pure White Hardy Water Lily)

planting.note: Set the rhizome horizontally in a wide planting basket of heavy garden soil capped with gravel, then lower the container so the crown rests 20 to 47 inches beneath the water surface in full sun.

directions: Introduced by the Latour-Marliac nursery in France in 1910, Virginalis remains one of the most widely grown pure-white hardy water lilies, producing enormous cup-shaped, slightly fragrant blooms of the purest white over pads 6 to 8 inches across. It is a vigorous, free-flowering variety well suited to medium to large ponds and lakes, tolerating deeper water than many hardy cultivars. Plant the rhizome horizontally in a wide aquatic basket of heavy loam topped with gravel in full sun, and divide every few years once the crown becomes crowded. Feed monthly during the growing season with aquatic fertilizer tablets for the longest, most reliable bloom season.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

common_name: Dauben Water Lily (Viviparous Pygmy Blue Tropical Water Lily)

planting.note: Plant tubers in heavy, fertile aquatic soil in a small submerged container once water has warmed well above 70F; Dauben tolerates as little as 4 hours of direct sun a day, making it useful for lower-light water gardens.

directions: Dauben (Nymphaea x daubenyana) traces to one of the very first man-made water lily hybrids, raised by Daubeny in 1863 from a cross involving the Egyptian blue lotus, Nymphaea caerulea, and the strongly viviparous Nymphaea micrantha. It is a compact, day-blooming tropical bearing small, star-shaped, light blue flowers held just above mottled green pads, and it is one of the easiest viviparous lilies to grow, freely producing plantlets directly from notches in its leaves. Its small size and shade tolerance make it a good choice for tubs, half-barrels, and small water gardens rather than large ponds. Because it is a true tropical, overwinter the tuber or a rooted plantlet indoors in moist sand once water temperatures drop in fall.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

common_name: Trudy Slocum Water Lily (Fragrant White Tropical Night-Blooming Water Lily)

planting.note: Plant tubers in heavy, fertile aquatic soil in submerged containers in a full-sun pond once the water has warmed well above 70F; site where evening blooms can be enjoyed after dusk.

directions: Trudy Slocum is a vigorous tropical night-blooming water lily bred by the Slocum family, producing profuse, nearly flat, pure white flowers 6 to 8 inches across held above nearly round, emerald-green pads mottled with purple blotches. Each pleasantly fragrant bloom opens at dusk and stays open until late the following morning, lasting three to four days before closing for good, and the plant flowers heavily from summer into fall. It is non-viviparous and best suited to medium to large water gardens where its spreading pads have room to develop. Because it is a true tropical, gardeners outside zones 9-11 should grow it as a warm-season annual or overwinter the dormant tuber indoors in damp sand.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

common_name: Emily Grant Hutchings Water Lily (Deep Pink Tropical Night-Blooming Water Lily)

planting.note: Plant tubers in heavy, fertile aquatic soil in submerged containers in a pond receiving at least a few hours of direct sun once the water has warmed well above 70F; site where evening blooms can be enjoyed after dusk.

directions: Bred by Gurney in 1922, Emily Grant Hutchings is a long-cultivated tropical night-blooming water lily with large, cup-shaped flowers in a rich deep pink to amaranth-red, opening after sunset and staying open into the following morning above bronze-green pads. It is a reliable, free-flowering older cultivar tolerant of somewhat lower light than many tropicals, needing as little as three hours of direct sun a day, and it performs well in medium to large ponds. Because it is a true tropical and not winter-hardy, gardeners outside zones 9-11 should grow it as a warm-season annual or lift and overwinter the dormant tuber indoors in moist sand once water temperatures fall. Feed monthly with aquatic fertilizer tablets through the growing season for the best evening display.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

common_name: Star of Siam Water Lily (Two-Tone Violet-Blue Tropical Water Lily)

planting.note: Plant tubers in heavy, fertile aquatic soil in submerged containers in a full-sun pond once the water has warmed well above 70F.

directions: Originating from Bangkok, Star of Siam is a popular tropical day-blooming water lily with star-shaped, two-tone violet-blue flowers roughly 6 inches across, their many modified stamens giving each bloom an unusually full, almost double appearance with white-tipped violet stamens at the center. The heavily maroon-and-green mottled pads make an attractive backdrop even before the fragrant flowers open each morning. It is a free-flowering, non-viviparous cultivar best suited to full sun and water 12 to 30 inches deep in a medium to large pond. As a true tropical it needs consistently warm water and should be grown as a seasonal annual or overwintered indoors as a dormant tuber outside zones 9-11.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

common_name: Innocence Water Lily (Large White Viviparous Tropical Water Lily)

planting.note: Plant tubers in heavy, fertile aquatic soil in submerged containers in a full-sun pond once the water has warmed well above 70F.

directions: Bred by Florida Aquatic Nurseries from an unnamed tropical hybrid crossed with 'Trail Blazer' (sharing a seed pod with the cultivar 'Carla's Sonshine'), Innocence is a tropical day-blooming water lily selected in 2001 and released in 2004 for its uniquely large, pure white flowers held high above the water on unusually robust stalks. Its pads are heavily mottled with maroon blotches over green, and the plant is strongly viviparous, readily producing new plantlets from notches along the leaf margins, which makes propagation easy. It is a medium to large, vigorous, free-flowering cultivar best grown in full sun in a medium to large pond. As a true tropical it should be grown as a seasonal annual or overwintered indoors as a dormant tuber outside zones 9-11.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

common_name: Charlene Strawn Water Lily (Fragrant Yellow Hardy Water Lily)

planting.note: Set the rhizome horizontally in a wide planting basket of heavy garden soil capped with gravel, then lower the container so the crown rests 12 to 24 inches beneath the water surface in full sun.

directions: Charlene Strawn is a hardy water lily hybrid between Nymphaea mexicana and Nymphaea odorata, notable for holding its rich yellow, strongly fragrant flowers well above the water surface on sturdy stems rather than resting flush with the pads, an unusual trait among hardy cultivars. Blooms fade to a lighter yellow on the outer petals as they age and are produced over a long season from early summer to early autumn. It is a moderately vigorous grower with rounded leaves to about 8 inches across, suited to ponds and lakes in full sun. Divide the rhizome every few years as the crown becomes crowded, and feed with aquatic fertilizer tablets through the growing season for the strongest bloom.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

common_name: Pink Platter Water Lily (Flat-Opening Medium Pink Tropical Water Lily)

planting.note: Plant tubers in heavy, fertile aquatic soil in submerged containers in a full-sun pond once the water has warmed well above 70F.

directions: Pink Platter is a free-flowering tropical day-blooming water lily named for the way its large, medium pink flowers open very flat, sitting above the pads like a platter rather than cupping upward. It is a vigorous, floriferous cultivar well suited to medium to large water gardens where its spreading pads have room to fill in. Grow in full sun in water 12 to 30 inches deep once temperatures have warmed well above 70F, feeding monthly with aquatic fertilizer tablets through the growing season for the heaviest bloom. As a true tropical it is not winter-hardy and should be grown as a warm-season annual or overwintered indoors as a dormant tuber outside zones 9-11.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society
